newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer Dome unveils offer for Bre-X Minerals.
newsitem.headline: Placer Dome unveils offer for Bre-X Minerals.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc., a Vancouver-based miner, said on Tuesday it presented a merger proposal to Bre-X Minerals Ltd., majority owner of the massive Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.

The Placer plan, sent to Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh from Placer Chief Executive John Willson in a letter dated Jan. 13, offered the Indonesian government up to a 40 percent equity interest in the Busang project.
It contemplates a stock-for-stock "merger of equals" at a "significant" premium to Bre-X's current share price.
Placer said it would not decide how many shares it would offer for Bre-X until after it negotiated with the company.

The Indonesian government is currently considering a joint venture proposal from Bre-X and Toronto-based Barrick Gold Corp., North America's largest gold producer and the partner the government selected for Bre-X.
The government has said it wanted a deal that would split the richest part of the Busang deposit with 67.5 percent for Barrick, 22.5 percent for Bre-X and 10 percent for Indonesia.

Busang is being touted as one of the richest gold finds in history and a number of companies in Indonesia and Canada have been involved in complex machinations to grab a significant part of its riches.

Under Placer's proposal, the Canadian miner would initiate the construction of a Busang mine and plant that would process up to 200,000 metric tons a day, costing up to $1.7 billion. Gold production would start in 1999 and average about three million to four million ounces a year.

The plan was subject to negotiation with Bre-X and the Indonesian government, due diligence, issuance of a contract of work for the project, resolution of all ownership issues and regulatory and shareholder approval, Placer said.
Willson said in the letter that Placer and Bre-X had been in continuous talks about a venture since October 1996.

"In October, you expressed interest in such a business combination, yet for various reasons, you indicated you were not able to give such a transaction serious consideration," Willson said in the letter.

"In light of the Barrick Gold proposal and the substantial uncertainty as to its implications for your shareholders, and our continuing strong interest in Busang, we are presenting this proposal now so that you and your board can fully evaluate the potential benefits this proposal provides to Bre-X shareholders," he added.

Placer said it would like to begin negotiations immediately to create a tax-effective, stock-for-stock "merger-of-equals" under which all of Bre-X's shares would be exchanged for a fixed number of Placer shares.

"We believe this proposal is compelling to your shareholders, providing them with a significant upfront premium while retaining the major upside potential of Busang through a widely held publicly traded Canadian company," Willson said in the letter.
